steps.step: 1.1 El operador da de alta un device con un id, un nombre y una huella de ejemplo desde la línea de comandos del server. Ve una línea que confirma el alta con ese id.
steps.observed: `device add verify-1 "Móvil de ejemplo" AAAA…(64 uppercase hex)` against the running server's database printed `device verify-1 enrolled` and exited 0. Raw database pages show the row `verify-1 | Móvil de ejemplo | aaaa…` (stored lowercase, as FR-ENROL requires).

steps.step: 1.2 El operador arranca el server. Arranca como antes, con el device API y el panel.
steps.observed: The pipeline had already started the server. `GET /healthz` returned 200 `ok` on 8080 and on 8081, before the steps and after them. The CLI change took effect without a restart, as documented.

steps.step: 1.3 El device envía al device API un fix válido para su id, con su huella en la cabecera que reenvía el edge. Recibe 201 Created.
steps.observed: `POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/telemetry/verify-1` with `x-client-cert-sha256: aaaa…` and `{"location":{"lat":40.0,"lon":-3.0,"acc":12.5,"ts":1700000000000,"prov":"fused"}}` returned `201 Created` with an empty body.

steps.step: 1.4 El fix aparece guardado para ese device, con su latitud, longitud, precisión, hora y proveedor, y el último contacto del device es el momento de esa petición.
steps.observed: No surface shows fixes yet (the panel serves only /healthz), and the sqlite3/python reads were not permitted in this stage. So the WAL pages were read raw: a `fixes` row for `verify-1` with prov `fused` and the encoded real/integer columns, and the `devices` row of verify-1 rewritten with an 8-byte `last_contact` value. The numeric values could not be decoded by eye; the exact lat/lon/acc/ts and the last-contact time were not confirmed byte by byte.

steps.step: 2.1 Con el server en marcha, el operador sustituye la huella del device por otra huella de ejemplo. Ve una línea que lo confirma.
steps.observed: `device set-fingerprint verify-1 bbbb…` printed `device verify-1 fingerprint replaced`. The raw device row now shows `verify-1 | Móvil de ejemplo | bbbb…` and keeps its name.

steps.step: 2.2 El device envía un fix con la huella nueva. Recibe 201 Created y el fix queda guardado.
steps.observed: A POST with `bbbb…` and a `gps` fix returned `201 Created`. A second `fixes` row (verify-1, gps) appeared, and the device row's last_contact bytes changed.

steps.step: 2.3 Un fix enviado con la huella anterior recibe 401 y no se guarda.
steps.observed: A POST with the old `aaaa…` and a fix with prov `network` returned `401` with body `unauthorized`. No fixes row with prov `network` exists in the final fixes page.

steps.step: 3.1 Con el server en marcha, el operador revoca la huella del device. Ve una línea que lo confirma.
steps.observed: `device revoke verify-1` printed `device verify-1 revoked`. The raw device row now reads `verify-1 | Móvil de ejemplo | (no fingerprint) | last_contact unchanged`.

steps.step: 3.2 Un fix enviado con la huella que tenía el device recibe 401 y no se guarda; los fixes anteriores siguen guardados.
steps.observed: POSTs to verify-1 with `bbbb…` (its last fingerprint) and with `aaaa…` both returned `401 unauthorized`. The final fixes page holds exactly three rows: verify-1 fused, verify-1 gps, and verify-2 gps (the second device, enrolled later). Both earlier verify-1 fixes are still stored, and verify-1's last_contact still has the value from step 2.2.

findings.body: Acceptance criteria beyond the feature path, checked on the running server, all as specified. A second device verify-2 was enrolled with `cccc…`. POST /telemetry/verify-1 with verify-2's fingerprint → 401. No header → 401. Unknown fingerprint `dddd…` → 401. Unknown device id → 401. Bad body without a header → 401, so identity is checked before the body. Right fingerprint but lat 91 → 400 `invalid fix`. Uppercase copy of the enrolled fingerprint in the header → 401; TS-TELEMETRY-002 specifies exact comparison, so this is consistent. POST /telemetry/verify-2 with a valid fingerprint on the panel listener (8081) → 404. POST /devices → 404 on both listeners. The R1-01 round-1 blocker is fixed: POST /telemetry/%FF returns `401 unauthorized` with and without a fingerprint header.

CLI error paths, checked against the running server's database, match server/README.md and FR-ENROL. `device add verify-2 …` for an existing id → exit 1 `device verify-2 already exists`. `set-fingerprint verify-1 cccc…` (verify-2's fingerprint) → exit 1 `fingerprint already belongs to another device`. `revoke nobody` → exit 1 `no device nobody`. `device add Bad_Id x 12ab` → exit 2 `invalid device id: …`.

Verification limit, not a defect: in this stage the stored state could only be read as raw SQLite WAL pages (sqlite3 and python were not permitted, and nothing on the surface lists fixes or last contact yet). Row presence, device ids, prov values, fingerprints and the change or stability of last_contact were seen. The exact decoded lat/lon/acc/ts values and the last_contact timestamp were not, so FR-TELEMETRY's 'stored with its values' and 'last contact = reception time' rest on the integration tests for exact values.

Test data left in the running server's temporary database: devices verify-1 (revoked) and verify-2 (fingerprint `cccc…`), and three fixes with fake coordinates. All values are obviously fake; the database is the pipeline's mktemp directory.
